messages:
matt (eng-ml): Hey – hitting a weird HF -> Redwood convert failure for a new model bring-up. `rw-convert` only sees 5/8 safetensors shards and then fails with weight key errors. The repo index.json on HF lists 8 siblings when viewed in the browser but our job logs show 5. Anyone seen a partial siblings listing before?

sara (eng-release): Link to the model + the convert command? any errors pasted? :eyes:

matt (eng-ml): Sure — model: https://huggingface.co/org/new-model/tree/main
Command I ran: ```bash
RW_TOKEN=$REDWOOD_KEY rw-convert hf://org/new-model --out /tmp/new-model-rw --quantize int8 --revision main
```
Logs: ```
2026-03-19T21:12:03Z import-bot: start job 4829
2026-03-19T21:12:04Z fetch: GET https://huggingface.co/api/models/org/new-model/siblings?revision=main -> 200 (Content-Length 1453)
2026-03-19T21:12:04Z fetch: parsed 5 siblings (safetensors-00001..-00005)
2026-03-19T21:12:05Z dl shard safetensors-00001 -> OK
2026-03-19T21:12:06Z dl shard safetensors-00002 -> 403 (expired token)
2026-03-19T21:12:07Z fallback: try anonymous -> only got 4 shards total
2026-03-19T21:12:08Z convert: KeyError missing weight key 'model.layers.10.attn.weight'
```
Feels like two problems: 1) the siblings API returned a truncated list (5) vs browser (8) and 2) token expiry mid-download caused some 403s.

kevin (eng-infra): Hmm. Could be HF CDN edge returning a cached listing (older index.json) or an incomplete response due to range/streaming. Also the 403 mid-download suggests our short-lived token is being rotated by the runner. Two quick checks: curl the raw siblings API from the same runner env + include `?revision=` explicitly, and check ETag/Cache-Control headers. Example: ```bash
curl -i "https://huggingface.co/api/models/org/new-model/siblings?revision=main"
```
Look for `etag` and `x-cache` headers.

julia (eng-ml): Adding: HF sometimes returns siblings arrays in multiple pages if there are lots of files, though usually not for 8 files. Another common gotcha: the hub-client will use your token to get presigned URLs for each shard; if the token in the runner is short-lived (we rotate every 30s on canaries), downloads can fail partway. Workaround for now: delete hub cache and force fresh auth, and pin revision to a git commit hash so the `siblings` response is stable.

matt (eng-ml): I re-ran from my laptop (no token rotation) with `--revision` set to the commit hash and `HF_TOKEN` exported. `curl` also showed different siblings lists from laptop vs runner (runner's response had Content-Length 900 and only 5 entries). Laptop: Content-Length 2178 and 8 entries. So likely an edge/cdn mismatch between the CI runner's CDN node and the origin.

import-bot: importer job 4829: retrying download of missing shards with fresh auth token

sara (eng-release): If it's CDN inconsistency we should add a retry/path to fetch missing siblings from origin (or try a different HF domain). Short-term: can you confirm that `rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface/hub` + setting HF_TOKEN to a long-lived PAT and pinning revision fixed the convert?

matt (eng-ml): Confirmed — after removing the hub cache and doing `export HF_TOKEN=xxxxxx` (long-lived) and `--revision=5a7b2c3` the convert completed: `converted 8/8 shards -> success, wrote new-model-rw/metadata.json`. No KeyError.

kevin (eng-infra): OK great. Longer-term action items: 1) runner should set an HF_TOKEN refresh window > job duration or fetch presigned urls atomically, 2) rw-convert should validate siblings count vs expected number in the index and fallback to origin if counts mismatch, 3) add a checksum fail-mode that re-queries siblings if any shard 403s. I'll file infra tasks.

julia (eng-ml): I'll add a small patch to the converter to treat `Content-Length` discrepancies and to re-pull siblings once before giving up. Also add a clear error message that suggests `--revision` pinning and `HF_TOKEN` advice.

matt (eng-ml): Thanks all — leaving this here in case someone else hits it. Posting the temporary reproducer in the ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-774

sara (eng-release): :100: good find. Marking as targeting 0.12.1 release notes (user-facing tip).
